# Contributing to ModDotPlot Browser

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

Thank you for improving ModDotPlot Browser. Correct and reproducible scientific output is
the project's first priority, followed by interactive performance and maintainability.

Start with the [design reference](docs/DESIGN.md),
[scientific specification](docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md), and applicable
[architectural decision records](docs/adr/).

## Development environment

Use the versions pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`, `.node-version`, `web/package.json`,
and both lockfiles. Install `wasm-pack`, then run:

```sh
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run dev
```

The browser bundle uses only static assets and browser APIs at runtime.

## Before submitting a change

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
cargo check -p moddotplot-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
npm --prefix web run verify
```

Keep changes modular, document public Rust APIs, and add focused unit tests for both
successful and erroneous input. Avoid unrelated formatting or generated-file changes.

## Scientific changes

A change is scientific if it affects sequence normalization, coordinates, hashing,
sketches, cardinality, containment, ANI conversion, strand evidence, sparse correction,
matrix boundaries, exact mode, missing values, or numeric tile contents.

Scientific changes must:

1. State the invariant or estimator being changed.
2. Add or update a simple exact/scalar reference implementation when possible.
3. Differentially test optimized output against that reference.
4. Include ambiguity, short-range, low-complexity, reverse-complement, and boundary
   cases relevant to the change.
5. Quantify approximation error and performance when an estimator changes.
6. Update `docs/DESIGN.md`, `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, and an ADR when
   the decision is durable.

Never loosen a correctness threshold to make an optimization pass without documenting
and scientifically justifying the changed error model.

The production backend is ntHash2 plus undensified OPH verified winners and HLL p10.
Exact canonical k-mer containment is the scientific oracle. Rejected minmer, bottom-s,
alternate-hash, densified, and inverted implementations are historical only and must
not be restored to the production surface without a reviewed ADR and new validation.

## Browser and renderer changes

Preserve the numeric tile contract and keep coloring in the renderer. Tile keys must
include every parameter that can change numeric output. A newly selected generation
must not accept stale tiles, and detailed computation must not delay presentation of a
complete quick viewport.

Test pure TypeScript state and parsing logic outside WebGL where possible. Renderer
changes should be manually checked in all supported desktop browser families until the
automated visual matrix is complete. Inspect pan, zoom, reset, resize, cache eviction,
self-comparison symmetry, exact zoom, and both color modes.

## Performance work

Benchmark the exact workload affected by the change. Report hardware, browser or
native target, build profile, input, parameters, elapsed time, and peak memory where
available. Keep raw machine-readable results beside the Markdown interpretation under
`docs/benchmarks/`.

An optimization is acceptable only after its numeric output passes the relevant
reference and statistical gates.

## Documentation and release notes

Update [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for user-visible changes. Documentation should call
zero-based and one-based coordinates explicitly, distinguish exact from estimated
values, and avoid claiming research validation until the gates in
[STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) are complete.
